verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The hexagram did not become a broadly recognized Jewish emblem until the early modern period, but its association with Jewish communities predates the seventeenth century. The Prague Jewish community was granted a flag bearing the symbol in 1354, and medieval synagogue and manuscript uses are documented. The categorical 'not associated until' claim is therefore false.

sources.title: Encyclopedia Judaica entry: Magen David
sources.relevance: Documents Jewish communal and synagogue uses in the fourteenth century, directly contradicting the claim of no association before the seventeenth century.

records.text: The Star of David is an occult symbol meant to represent King Solomon's ring.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: The Star of David, as they term it, is in fact an occult symbol meant to represent King Solomon's ring.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 12:04. Historical sources confirm that hexagrams and pentagrams were associated with the legendary Seal of Solomon and magical traditions, but the modern Star of David has a broader, distinct history as a Jewish communal and religious symbol. Calling it simply an occult symbol 'meant' to represent Solomon's ring is reductive.

sources.title: What Is the Seal of Solomon? - Chabad.org
sources.relevance: Explains the magical Seal of Solomon tradition while distinguishing historical meanings from the broader Jewish Star of David.

records.text: Wikipedia says the Seal of Solomon is often depicted as a hexagram or pentagram and was associated with supernatural power and medieval and Renaissance magic.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It is quite literally known as the Seal of Solomon. I'm going to show you this. This is on Wikipedia. ... This is that accessible. We can read parts of this together. It reads, it is often depicted in the shape of either a hexagram or a pentagram. ... In mystic Jewish lore, the ring is variously described as having been given Solomon the power to command the supernatural. ... Due to the proverbial wisdom of Solomon, it came to be seen as an amulet or a talisman or a symbol or character in medieval magic and Renaissance magic, occultism, alchemy.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 12:16. The cited Seal of Solomon page says it is often a hexagram or pentagram, attributes supernatural powers to Solomon's ring in mystical lore, and describes associations with medieval/Renaissance magic, occultism, and alchemy.
